title: Independent Sales Agent Program
meta_description: Partner with MCCPS as an independent sales agent or ISO and earn residuals on the merchants you bring. See how the program works and what support you get.
dek: Bring merchants to MCCPS, earn residuals while they process, and lean on a team that handles underwriting, support and statements.
intro: Merchant services is a relationship business. A merchant who trusts the person who recommended their processor tends to stay with them, and that long tail is what makes the agent model attractive. If you already talk with business owners, whether you are an accountant, a consultant, a POS reseller or a full-time salesperson, you may be positioned to help them and be paid for it.

MCCPS recruits independent sales agents and ISOs who earn residuals on the merchants they bring. This page explains how the model works, what support is on offer and what to think through before you join. Nothing here is a promise of income.

paragraphs: When a merchant processes cards, the processor earns revenue on each transaction. A residual is the share of that ongoing revenue paid to the agent who brought the merchant, typically for as long as the merchant keeps processing under the agreement. The payments recur monthly and move up and down with the merchant's volume.

That structure means income is not immediate or guaranteed. It builds as merchants are approved, go live and process, and it depends on their volume, the pricing, merchant retention and the terms of your agent agreement. No example earnings are offered here, because results vary widely.

Merchant attrition matters as well. Merchants close, change processors or reduce volume, and a portfolio needs ongoing attention to stay healthy. Agents who check in with their merchants, answer questions and stay useful tend to retain them better than those who disappear after onboarding.

sections.h2: Agent, ISA and ISO: the roles
paragraphs: An independent sales agent, sometimes called an ISA, finds merchants and refers or enrolls them with a processor that handles the underwriting and support. An ISO, or independent sales organization, is a registered entity that may manage agents, hold relationships with acquiring banks and take on more responsibility.

MCCPS processes through registered ISOs of several banks, which allows it to offer merchants a range of solutions. Our guides on ISO versus agent roles and on what an ISO is cover the distinction in detail.

Partners get a complete solution to offer: free statement analysis, the Zero Processing Fees program where eligible, PCI compliance help, next-day funding availability, multiple gateways, B2B Level 2 and Level 3 processing, EMV and contactless, and integration with almost any POS, smartphone or terminal. Merchants also receive free 24/7 technical support and personal customer service.

That matters because agents are judged by what happens after the sale. When a merchant has a terminal problem at night, the support burden does not fall on you. The reporting and analytics dashboard in PayPilot by MCCPS also gives merchants a reason to stay engaged.

paragraphs: The most effective approach is to lead with a free analysis rather than a pitch. Ask for two months of statements, review them line by line, and show the owner what they pay. Owners respond to clarity, and the review often reveals fees they did not know about.

Be careful with promises. Never guarantee savings, and never claim a rate before the review. Explain that dual pricing, cash discounting and surcharging rules vary by state and card network and require proper disclosure. Honest, informed advice wins repeat referrals. Our guide on using statement analysis to win merchants goes further.

Build a simple process: a short intro conversation, a request for statements, a clear review meeting and a written follow-up. Keep notes on each prospect, including the date of their contract renewal, since timing is often what decides whether a merchant can move.

Agents represent MCCPS and the banks behind it, so conduct matters. That means accurate descriptions of products and fees, no misleading comparisons, careful handling of merchant data and respect for privacy rules. Complete applications honestly, because misstatements can cause problems for the merchant.

Agents also must follow applicable laws, which differ by state, and the terms of the partner agreement. Consult your attorney or accountant about licensing, tax treatment and business structure for your own situation.

Check that your marketing materials match what MCCPS offers. Describe the Zero Processing Fees program as a compliant dual-pricing or cash-discount approach whose rules vary by state and card network, and never present it as available to every business.

sections.h2: Who tends to be a good fit
paragraphs: Good candidates are people with trusted access to business owners: accountants and bookkeepers, business brokers, POS and software resellers, web designers, insurance agents and independent salespeople. You do not need a payments background, but you do need patience for a relationship-driven sale and an interest in learning how fees work.
Think about your time. Prospecting, follow-up and merchant onboarding take effort, and some months produce little. Treat it as a business, set realistic expectations and track your pipeline.

Call 844.826.6227 to speak with someone about the program, ask about the agreement, and learn how onboarding and residual reporting work. Read the agent agreement carefully, including term, residual structure, payment timing and what happens if a merchant leaves.
If you want a feel for the product first, send your own business's statements for the free analysis. Seeing the process from the merchant's side makes you a more credible advocate.

key_takeaways: Residuals are ongoing payments tied to merchant processing volume.
Income is variable and no earnings are promised or implied.
MCCPS handles underwriting, support and statements for referred merchants.
Lead with a free analysis and honest advice, never guaranteed savings.

faq.a: No, but you need to learn how fees work and enjoy relationship selling. MCCPS provides product information and support. Your background in working with business owners is the main asset.

faq.q: What is the difference between an agent and an ISO?
faq.a: An agent finds merchants and refers or enrolls them with a processor. An ISO is a registered organization with bank relationships that may manage agents and carry more responsibility. Roles vary by arrangement.

It varies widely and is not guaranteed. Earnings depend on merchant volume, pricing, retention and your agreement. No figures are offered here as typical. Review the agreement carefully before deciding.
MCCPS offers free 24/7 technical support and personal customer service to merchants, plus a reporting dashboard. That reduces the support burden on you as an agent.

faq.q: Can I be an agent while keeping another job?
faq.a: Many partners do, as long as the agreement and any employer obligations allow it. Consider time, conflicts of interest and licensing. Consult your attorney or accountant about your situation.
